[[File:Giggledust-AoD.png|thumb|200px|A container of the spice variant [[Giggledust]]]]
{{Quote|Glitterstim's all right if you're blue. Everything takes on a rise, a buzz, a life, as if your whole body had been made new and your whole future with it.|[[Greglik]]|<ref name="Planet of Twilight">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref>}}
'''Spice''', also known as '''narco-spice''',<ref name="GG6-2">[[Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters'', Second Edition]]</ref> was slang for various mind-altering drugs. Varieties included [[Ryll/Legends|ryll]] and the strongest (and most expensive), [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]]. The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] was rich with these spices, which were harvested from dangerous mines, at one point in history by [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] labor. [[Sevarcos II]], [[Rori/Legends|Rori]], [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]], [[Gargon/Legends|Gargon]], and [[Mon Gazza/Legends|Mon Gazza]] were other sources of spice. The word could also refer to non-narcotic herbs and minerals used to give [[Foodstuff/Legends|foods]] or drinks flavor.

==Etymology==
The term ''spice'' referred to any substances (either organically produced or mined minerals) that were ingestible, but not consumed for nutrition as food. Usually they could be added to food for seasoning and preservation while some had medicinal properties or enhanced bodily functions and experiences. The latter were used for their recreational effects, but they included dangerous intoxicants that caused addiction and deemed illegal.<ref name="SOTE guide" />

One substance could have multiple uses: [[Andris/Legends|Andris]] was commonly used as food condiment and had beneficient effects, but other variants were addictive and were illegal, available only in the [[Black market/Legends|black market]]. Meanwhile, spices had different effects throughout different [[species/Legends|species]]: although [[salt/Legends|salt]] was a common seasoning, it was addictive to the [[Arcona/Legends|Arcona]] (and they smuggled it as a narcotic<ref>{{Hnn|55|regional/1359_2.html|Arconan Smuggling Cartel Dismantled}}</ref>). As such, the meaning of the catch-all term ''spice'' was nebulous.<ref name="SOTE guide">''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]''</ref>

By extension, ''spice'' was figuratively any small luxury that added variety to life, such as wealth and entertainment.<ref name="SOTE guide" />

==History==
[[File:Spice_processing_LoNH.png|thumb|left|200px|Spice being processed]]
Spice was known to have gained widespread use since the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], even before [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]]. 

Most forms of spice were collected raw, then processed and refined. Some forms of spice were produced completely synthetically, without the use of any kind of natural material. Many organizations, and planets, took on this enterprise, notably the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]].

The spice found on Kessel was [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]], one of the most prized spices in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. This particular spice was created by a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[energy spider]]s that would spin the spice into webs. Any unlucky miner that came into contact with one of these creatures would have their life energy sucked out of them in seconds.

Glitterstim was mined on [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] by criminals. Since Kessel lay within the [[Maw Cluster/Legends|Maw Cluster]], in the unlikely event a prisoner were to escape they would not likely go far because of the surrounding [[Maw Cluster/Legends|black holes]]. Kessel had no natural [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], and factories on the surface created air; however, the air was still too thin to breathe without an [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]] mask. Glitterstim was activated by light, forcing workers to work in complete darkness or under dim, [[Color/Legends|red]] lights that lacked photons energetic enough to trigger it.<ref name="The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett">{{StoryCite|story=The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> Along with the obvious dangers of energy spiders, glitterstim threads were very sharp, and could easily remove digits if the worker was not careful.<ref name="The Paradise Snare">''[[The Paradise Snare]]''</ref>

Another kind of spice was [[ryll]], mined on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], noted by its medicinal properties.<ref name="guide" />

The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] attempted to keep a tight rein on the circulation of the various forms of spice, making it a frequent item for [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]. Smuggling spice (buying without a receipt or transporting without a permit) was a class four violaton of the [[Imperial Code]], punishable with a month in [[prison/Legends|prison]] and a fine, which could reach up to 5,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Credits]]. Possession and trafficking of illegal or restricted spice were violations of higher class with more severe punishment, including impounding of property and loss of certification; the penalty for transporting [[carsunum]], for example, could reach 30 years in prison and a fine of 10,000.<ref name="guide">''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]''</ref>

Almost every inhabited [[star system/Legends|star system]] had various regulations on spice possession or transportation; violation of local customs was a class five infraction according to the Imperial Code, fined between 100 and 5,000 Credits.<ref name="guide" />

Spice markets could be found on [[Shadowport/Legends|shadowports]]; [[the Life]] section of the [[Vergesso Base]] shadowport had a notable spice market.<ref name="guide" />

In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] bought the spice mines of Kessel.

The illegal spice market was virtually destroyed as a result of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. With the Hutts attempting to fight off the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], their contacts were stripped of their connection. Many people were forced to confront their addictions, and spice all but lost its worth. By at least [[130 ABY]], the spice trade had been rebuilt.

[[Wendell Wright-Sims]] was a [[Drug dealer]] of spice.

==Behind the scenes==
It has been posited that [[W:c:dune:Frank_Herbert|Frank Herbert's]] classic science fiction novel [[W:c:dune:Dune_(novel)|''Dune'' (1965)]] had a heavy influence upon ''Star Wars''. The drug known as [[W:c:dune:Spice_Melange|"the spice" ''Melange'']] plays a central role in the Duniverse.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-dune-story-concepts-ideas-lucas-copy|text=Everything Star Wars Took From Dune|author=Lethbridge, Thomas|date=2021-10-20|quote=However, perhaps because of its shared genre, the book's most obvious descendent is probably the ''Star Wars'' universe. In fact, in the 2003 Herbert biography ''Dreamer of Dune'', written by his son Brian, it is claimed that ''"(Herbert) & the other science fiction writers who thought they saw their work in Lucas's movie formed a loose organization that my father called, with his tongue firmly placed in his cheek, the We're Too Big to Sue George Lucas Society."'' This demonstrates the clear parallels that Herbert himself saw between his work and the ''Star Wars'' movies. Upon closer inspection, it's clear that he may have had a claim. Here is everything that ''Star Wars'' took from ''Dune.'' (...) One of the most important plot points in ''Dune'' is the so-called spice melange, a mind-altering substance that allows for interstellar travel and that's only known source – at least in the first book – is the planet Arrakis. Possession of the spice influences everything in the world of ''Dune'' and is one of the factors that shapes the Harkonnen/Atreides feud at the center of the narrative. Although the spice of ''Star Wars'' is not as significant to the overall plot as the spice of Arrakis, George Lucas' films do feature so-called spice mines on the planet Kessel, highlighting a clear connection between the two works.|work=''[[Wikipedia:Screen Rant|Screen Rant]]''|archivedate=20211029072532}}</ref> Spice was first mentioned at the beginning of the [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|original ''Star Wars'']] with C-3PO's worry to R2-D2 that "''We'll be sent to the Spice Mines of Kessel, smashed into who-knows-what!''"

The concept of spice in the ''Star Wars'' universe appeared for the first time in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] and is only mentioned briefly by C-3PO and Luke.

Since then spice has appeared in countless [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] works, and is even mentioned briefly in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].

Prior to the ''New Game Enhancements'' introduced to ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', spice was a consumable within the game that players who chose the smuggler profession could craft. Once ingested, it would improve a certain number of stats at the cost of decreasing others. After the effect wore off, you would experience spice withdrawal for several minutes, prompting your character to appear to vomit and lowering all of your stats.

Author [[Kevin J. Anderson]] noted that some "politically correct" individuals at Lucasfilm almost forced him to characterize spice as a food additive in ''[[Jedi Search]]'' out of concern for characterizing Han as a drug dealer during his smuggling days. The matter was brought up to [[George Lucas]], who confirmed that spice is a drug. Anderson compromised by adding positive qualities to the substance instead of categorizing it as a damaging substance like [[Wikipedia:Crystal meth|crystal meth]].<ref name="dwolver">{{WebCite|url=http://www.alternativenation.net/interview-star-wars-author-kevin-j-anderson-recounts-jedi-academy-trilogy-darksaber-tales-jedi|text=Interview: Star Wars Author Kevin J. Anderson On 'Jedi Academy Trilogy', 'Darksaber', & 'Tales of the Jedi'|archivedate=20160113032611}}</ref>
